column8: Fri 20 Nov: 3c and 3e pedigree for why the central top uses the compound 7.5%, the median path; every finance judge knows it, so one clause at most; say compound, never average (row 30).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, the founder of the compound-rate rule fenced it off from unique choices, so the 7.5% marks the middle of her one run, never where she lands; page not seen; sits beside Q123-006, a different source for a near point.

Fri 20 Nov: gloss on IPS l.11 for 3a or 3f: a man who lacks a fixed sum he needs may rightly gamble, Laura owns hers so has no reason to; links to NUMBERS 8s (the first plan had to buy all ten on 1 Jan 2033 with whatever shares had become); quote checked for page before use.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 2 note: J.P. Morgan's own handbook says the compound column fits a single asset, and VT is the plan's only forecast; one clause, pedigree with a point (no blended portfolio return to quote).

Fri 20 Nov: numbers owner note, not report text: 17.88% is the spread of simple yearly returns and J.P. Morgan's three figures fit a lognormal exactly; never derive 7.5% in the report; Keel arithmetic, S 3.

Fri 20 Nov: wording guard: never 'the gap is half the variance' as exact (1.60 against the published 1.44); also marks Q6b-017's and Q123-020's half-variance conversions as shortcuts; quote J.P. Morgan's published compound figure only.
Fri 20 Nov: textbook; useful only if 3e or Table 2's note must say why two figures exist; one plain sentence, otherwise left out.
Fri 20 Nov: the arithmetic behind row 31; NUMBERS 4's 4%-10% table already shows it (9% column: unrounded top $117,972, stated $115,000); Keel arithmetic on house inputs, never a plan figure.

Fri 20 Nov: the 26.2% omits the excess, and the critique is false: the excess rises with VT (NUMBERS 4: $7,503 at 7.5%, $8,358 at 9%; half kept plus excess $31,057 at 9%), so the mean-path cover is about 27%; the point stands only as say about 25%, if shares earn the 7.5% assumed (8u).

Fri 20 Nov: true count, wrong use: a top built on 8.94% would still state $115,000 (rows 8 and 31), so never say it is a figure most futures miss or that co-sponsors are better served; use only as why 3e quotes the compound column; Keel arithmetic, never a plan figure.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c's pre-move percentages: the wrong column would overstate how often the top is reached by about 5 points; the plan's figure stays NUMBERS 8p's 35.4% and section 4's 57.2%, the 34% and 29% are Keel arithmetic only.

Fri 20 Nov: an ergodicity restatement (average across worlds, not people) in H5-002's place; 'no investor and no pool of investors earns it' overstates, since a one-year holder's expected return is 8.94%; reasoning only.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, the drag can blur only pencil; fix: never call the late-2032 fund's payout fixed (NUMBERS 0) or a stated end one that cannot move (an early fund end at zero interest can leave the top short, NUMBERS 3); say the stated end, counted on its holdings with no further interest; the turn only pencil has two averages goes to CONCEIT's store, 3c's one turn is two inkings, two dates; Chambers and Zdanowicz's limit case is a loose parallel.
Fri 20 Nov: the same idea as row 13 dated at the move; the move's timing is already told by ownership (spine rows 1 and 7), so no separate row.
Fri 20 Nov: pedigree only: the constant-mix result does not describe VT, which is cap-weighted and never rebalanced (row 21), so the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy; abstract only.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e and 3f's copout clause: diversification lifts the typical future, not expected wealth, and a single run lives the typical one; verified quote; one clause, with row 21's buy-and-hold mechanism.
Fri 20 Nov: cleanest illustration of drag alone (same average, slower middle) for 3e or 3f; J.P. Morgan's assumptions, never history; the 1.7% is Keel arithmetic.

Fri 20 Nov: TNA l.23's winners are companies and these rows are markets, and the gap is 0.3% over three years, so never call it the price (price is kept for a dollar cost with its model named); an illustration of J.P. Morgan's table only; Keel arithmetic.

Fri 20 Nov: keep the guard (most, never any: Japan and US minimum volatility drag less), but fix the critique: the world's 1.44 against US large caps' 1.45 is a rounding tie at two decimals, so never 'less drag than US shares'; EAFE and emerging are regions, not single markets.
Fri 20 Nov: reference data for row 19 and a judge's question; the four exhibits are fixed, so no new exhibit; note the world and US large cap tie and no Taiwan row.
Fri 20 Nov: correct mechanism for VT (winners grow inside a never-rebalanced cap-weighted fund); stops any rebalancing bonus being claimed; one clause at most beside row 16.

Fri 20 Nov: 3f copout clause: the mechanism and the median (-2.29%) behind Q46-002 and Q175-009's counts; never repeat the headline counts as new; the monthly-against-yearly comparison stated as such.

Fri 20 Nov: use the exact world drag (1.44, row 6), state the same-average assumption, illustrative swings only, never a measured cost for any named stock; in 3f the team's reason stays its own words (standing order 22, told truthfully), this is a later clause of analysis, never what the team computed then.
Fri 20 Nov: the +50%/-40% coin is H5-002's coin; Hakansson's quote adds pedigree with no part to serve; infinite-sequence results against a three- and five-year run.

Fri 20 Nov: never 'optimal' in the report, even quoted; the 100% riskless corner is an artefact of the normal curve, so the parallel to a missed payment breaks under its own disanalogy; read only through a search excerpt.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c, before the move only: the central top on today's figures is a median and blind to a crash, so the owned bottom and Table 2's spread answer it; after the move the top is owned, not a median, and framing D (Laura names the top) stands.
Fri 20 Nov: twin of Q123-006 (the log rule is one taste among many); preface OCR partly unreadable.
Fri 20 Nov: serves no part, since the report never derives 7.5% (row 6); abstract only, via a search copy.

Fri 20 Nov: numbers owner note, never a re-size: the engine reads 17.88% as a log spread, wider than J.P. Morgan's (about 16.3%), so the register's share risk is cautious; NUMBERS 8p's 'on J.P. Morgan's 7.5% and 17.88%' is the engine's reading; Q61-017's 16.3% is J.P. Morgan's basis; code read and Keel arithmetic.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e and Table 2's note: say grows 7.5% a year, compounded, never averages 7.5%; flags CANON B15's gloss (average yearly) for the lead, since the plain yearly average is 8.94%; stronger twin of Q37-012; the TNA's about 7.5% a year stays as frozen; never a median figure for the panel.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e's one line on which column: the stated range is the same on either column on today's figures (NUMBERS 4's 4%-10% table); say 'once stated' for no stated figure depends on shares, and the drag reaches only the top she will be able to state and her flexibility; Keel arithmetic, never a plan figure.
